name: Doromu-Koki
confidence_why: 4 independent first-hand sources agree (3 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant' penultimate (penultimate stress) rests on a 2022 713-pp reference-grammar dissertation by the long-term fieldworker; the quotation is verbatim at sec. 2.5.1 p. 125 of the PDF downloaded now, and two earlier SIL phonology descriptions by the same author (2002, 2010) say the same. Nothing better exists in Glottolog's list. One optional refinement, not a reclassify: the record's domain is not yet coded, but the source is explicit that enclitics and verbal suffixes do not shift stress (['jɑβɑ=ɾi], ['nĩ-bo-bi-ɡɛdi-mɑ̃]) and that the stress domain is the phonological word excluding enclitics (sec. 2.8.1 p. 133), so the domain field could be filled as root/stem-penult with unstressed clitics/suffixes; 'dominant' rather than 'strict' is consistent with that. Also note the thesis's own ch. 2 summary (p. 141) misprints 'Stress is phonemic', contradicted by 2.5.1; cite 2.5.1 only.

sources.citation: Bradshaw 2022, A grammar of Doromu-Koki, PhD thesis JCU, sec. 2.5.1 (full PDF researchonline.jcu.edu.au/75450 re-read)
sources.quote: Stress is not phonemic, always occurring on the penultimate syllable in words of two or more syllables or otherwise on the ultimate syllable. Stress does not shift with the addition of a clitic or verbal suffix.

sources.citation: Bradshaw, Robert L. 2002. Doromu organised phonology data. SIL-PNG ms., 5 pp. (Internet Archive copy of www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/pubs/0000087/Doromu (Koki))
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Stress is predictable. It occurs on the penultimate syllable.' with examples 'bu, 'buku, i'boka.

sources.citation: Bradshaw, Robert L. 2022. A grammar of Doromu-Koki: a Papuan language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, James Cook University. DOI 10.25903/b4c6-x282. 713 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p.125: 'Stress is not phonemic, always occurring on the penultimate syllable in words of two or more syllables or otherwise on the ultimate syllable. Stress does not shift with the addition of a clitic or verbal suffix.' p.133: 'stress primarily occurs on the penultimate syllable. Postpositional enclitics, which bear no stress, are regularly attached to the final constituent in a noun phrase'; compounds/reduplications 'maintain their individual stress'. Examples ['jɑβɑ=ɾi], ['nĩ-bo-bi-ɡɛdi-mɑ̃] show stress fixed on the root penult (or sole root syllable), not recomputed over clitics/verbal suf
sources.locator: sec. 2.5.1 p. 125; also sec. 1.3 p. 78, sec. 2.8.1 p. 133, ch. 2 summary p. 141
